title: C and N
summary: Down to the bottom row, and the last of the very common consonants.
intro: Everything you have reached for so far has been above the home row. C and N go the other way, and the movement is different: the finger curls under rather than stretching out, and the hand wants to drop with it. Keep the wrist where it is and let the finger travel alone. N is the sixth most common letter in English, so this reach is one of the most valuable in the course.
congrats: You now have every letter in and, in, on, no, not and can — the joints that hold English sentences together. The bottom row is the least comfortable row on the keyboard, and you have just made a start on it.

screens.text: Left middle finger, curling down and slightly inward from D. It is a shorter movement than it looks — if you are moving your whole hand, you are reaching too far.
C and D, down and back. The middle finger now covers three rows on its own.

screens.text: Right index finger, down and inward from J. Your busiest finger takes on a sixth key — and this one is worth the trouble, because N turns up in almost every sentence.
N and J. Curl the finger down rather than pushing the hand forward, and let it come back to the bump every time.
screens.content:

jhun uhnj
knj hfd kn

screens.text: Both new keys against their home keys. This is the drill that teaches the return — do it slowly enough that you feel the bump each time.
screens.content:
jc cj jcjc
nnn cccc dddd jjjj
cncn ncnc

screens.text: The same movement under a little time pressure. Accuracy first; the clock is there for rhythm, not for speed.
N first, because you will type it more than almost anything else. Watch for the nd and in pairs — they come up constantly.
screens.content:

screens.text: Now C, which rarely stands alone: it arrives with H, K or L right behind it more often than not.
screens.content:

screens.text: Short words with both keys. If your hand lifts off the home row between words, you are working harder than you need to.
Twenty-one keys, mixed. Most of the words on this screen were impossible for you two lessons ago.
screens.content:
hi reads saw grid health
other shakes slight do fun
sled world crowd those touch

screens.text: Sentences with real grammar in them now, not just strings of nouns. Keep your eyes a word ahead of your hands.
screens.content:
the story is worth it
you can learn this in one hour
they wrote two short letters

screens.text: Last screen. Next lesson finishes the bottom row for your index and middle fingers.
